title: State (BSES YPL) v. Gaffar Miya (FIR 461/2019)
court: Addl. Sessions Judge-05 (Electricity), East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
result: Gaffar Miya convicted under Section 135, Electricity Act, 2003; co-accused Sonia (visiting daughter) dropped u/s 258 Cr.P.C.; civil liability (theft bill Rs. 60,536) settled during trial; posted for hearing on sentence
statutes: Third proviso to Section 135(1) Electricity Act 2003

interpretations.interpretation: Clause (a) — tapping or making a connection with a licensee's lines — is the operative limb in a direct-hooking case. 'Dishonestly' being undefined in the Act, Section 24 IPC supplies the definition (wrongful gain/wrongful loss); drawing supply through an unmetered illegal Teflon-wire tap from the input terminal of another consumer's meter satisfies dishonest intention.

Reverse-onus clause: proof of an artificial or unauthorised means of abstraction raises a presumption of dishonest use 'until the contrary is proved'. 'Shall presume' is compulsory (Neeraj Dutt); rebuttal standard is evidence making the defence reasonably probable to a prudent man (Hiten P. Dalal); natural rebuttal is proof of lawful metered use — paid bills — the onus lying on the consumer under Section 106 Evidence Act (Mukesh Rastogi).

Reg. 60: inspection power (suo motu or on information) with photo-ID safeguards. Reg. 61: contemporaneous inspection report, seizure/sealing, photo/video documentation. Reg. 62: prosecution only where dishonest intention evident; disconnection + police complaint within 24 hours; missing seal alone insufficient. Reg. 63: assessment at twice tariff for up to 12 months with credit for paid units. Unchallenged compliance confirms regularity of inspection.

citations.case: Sonu @ Amar v. State of Haryana
citations.principle: Objection that an electronic record was admitted without a Section 65B certificate goes to the mode of proof and must be raised when the record is tendered; if not taken at trial it cannot be raised later.

citations.case: Balu Sudam Khalde v. State of Maharashtra
citations.principle: Incriminating suggestions put by defence counsel in cross-examination bind the accused and can establish facts such as the factum of, and presence at, the inspection.

citations.case: Punjab State Electricity Board v. Ashwani Kumar
citations.principle: An inspection report prepared by officers in discharge of official duty carries a presumption of regularity; onus on the consumer to rebut by cogent evidence.

citations.case: Sushil Sharma v. BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd.
citations.principle: Non-examination of an independent/public witness is no infirmity where inspecting officials are trustworthy and bear no enmity to the accused.
'Shall presume' denotes a compulsory legal presumption the court is bound to draw until the fact is disproved.

citations.case: Hiten P. Dalal v. Bratindranath Banerjee
citations.principle: Rebuttal of a statutory presumption need not be conclusive; evidence must make the defence reasonably probable to a prudent man.

citations.case: Mukesh Rastogi v. North Delhi Power Ltd.
citations.principle: Easiest rebuttal of the theft presumption is production of paid electricity bills; Section 106 Evidence Act places that onus on the consumer.

significance.point: Mere presence at the raided premises is not culpability
significance.explanation: The visiting married daughter found at the spot — who even falsely called herself a tenant — was dropped u/s 258 Cr.P.C.; liability confined to the person shown to be abstracting and using the electricity.
Absence of a 65B certificate for inspection videography is not fatal where the defence did not object when the electronic record was tendered (Sonu @ Amar).

significance.point: Defence cross-examination can prove the case
significance.explanation: Incriminating suggestions put by defence counsel — that the wires ran from the running ground-floor meter's input terminal — can themselves establish the factum of inspection and bind the accused (Balu Sudam Khalde).

significance.point: The reverse-onus presumption does real work
significance.explanation: Once an unauthorised means of abstraction is proved, the 'shall presume' clause compels a presumption of dishonest theft; rebuttal requires evidence of a lawful metered source — typically paid bills under the Section 106 onus (Mukesh Rastogi).

significance.point: A public witness is not essential
significance.explanation: Non-joining of an independent witness does not vitiate an otherwise trustworthy official inspection (Ashwani Kumar; Sushil Sharma).

significance.point: Settling the theft bill can cut against the accused
significance.explanation: Payment of the civil liability during trial was read as conduct corroborating guilt on the criminal charge.

generic_facts.theft_mode: direct theft / hooking — no meter at premises; Teflon wires tapped from input terminal of another user's ground-floor meter

generic_facts.meter_status: no meter installed for inspected premises
generic_facts.occupant_at_inspection: accused's married daughter (Sonia), falsely claiming to be a tenant; visiting from matrimonial home
key_evidence: seized Teflon wires produced in court
